answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil swarms via proof-of-space, requiring each candidate vertex to allocate dedicated storage sectors. Nodes must answer random disk-read challenges signed by a cryptographic quill, refracting verification through a multi-agent prism. An attacker incurs unshareable hardware capacity and drive bandwidth costs per identity. However, this mechanism disadvantages lightweight edge agents and cannot deter well-funded entities leasing bulk data center storage.
